# Assessing The Fantasy Basketball Production Of NBA Rookies

Locked On Fantasy Basketball, 2026-09-03, 31:18. https://youtu.be/OBwWCxG9SqM

## Summary

Josh Lloyd looks at how NBA rookies have done in fantasy since the 2020-21 season, then ranks the 2026 rookie class. Over six seasons only four rookies finished top 50 per game in category leagues and 16 finished top 100. About twice as many become relevant over the final two months of the season. Yahoo ADP puts far too many rookies in the top 150, so people take too many late-round rookie flyers. He sees Cameron Boozer as clearly the best fantasy rookie and Caleb Wilson as second. He thinks Darryn Peterson and especially AJ Dybantsa are drafted too high. He calls Darius Acuff Jr., Mikel Brown Jr., Jax Lenderborg and Johnson Jr. fine late flyers, and advises against Keaton Wagler. He also notes the Clippers' penalty and expects the Kawhi Leonard to Toronto trade to go through.

## Rules and methods

- [4:24](https://youtu.be/OBwWCxG9SqM?t=264) Be cautious about investing in rookies in fantasy drafts.
  > "when we're talking about rookies in fantasy, we have to be very cautious about how we invest in them"
- [7:09](https://youtu.be/OBwWCxG9SqM?t=429) The number of relevant rookies goes up in the second half of the season and fantasy playoffs. The causes are tanking, injuries and rookies improving.
  > "the last half of the season in your fantasy playoffs, the number of relevant rookies increases,"
- [7:53](https://youtu.be/OBwWCxG9SqM?t=473) The rookie wall and the sophomore slump are lazy narratives. He says most rookies and second-year players get better, so do not treat these as general rules.
  > "season goes on. Oh, sophomore slump. Yeah, except again 90% of second year players get better."
- [10:56](https://youtu.be/OBwWCxG9SqM?t=656) With less tanking expected this season, the late-season jump in rookie relevance may be smaller than usual.
  > "we get double the amount of rookies becoming relevant, I I don't think it's going to be as extreme"
- [13:57](https://youtu.be/OBwWCxG9SqM?t=837) ADP overrates rookies mostly in the late flyer range. Drafters take far too many rookies near the end of drafts, when most classes give only about three or four relevant players.
  > "we take too many rookies towards the end of a draft when in reality where there's probably going to be"
- [19:58](https://youtu.be/OBwWCxG9SqM?t=1198) Rookies, especially rookie guards, usually shoot badly for the first two to three months and then improve.
  > "He will have bad shooting numbers for two to three months, but it will trend up and get better."
- [21:55](https://youtu.be/OBwWCxG9SqM?t=1315) Judge a rookie by situation, minutes, usage and non-scoring stats, not by draft position.
  > "look at the situation on the team. Where is he going to slide in usage-wise, minutes wise?"
- [23:17](https://youtu.be/OBwWCxG9SqM?t=1397) Projections have to assume trade candidates stay all season. This can understate the rookies behind them.
  > "you sort of do have to project it out assuming that Sabonis and Lavine are going to be there all season"
- [24:08](https://youtu.be/OBwWCxG9SqM?t=1448) If a drafted rookie starts with real usage but hurts your efficiency, hold him until about Thanksgiving before giving up.
  > "if you draft rookies, especially rookie guards, give them until Thanksgiving. If they're starting and they got a usage role"
- [28:01](https://youtu.be/OBwWCxG9SqM?t=1681) Do not hold several inefficient rookie flyers at once while waiting for them to improve. Pick which ones to keep and drop the rest quickly.
  > "you can't hold all of them through to Thanksgiving or else you'll be, you know, six weeks in"
- [30:07](https://youtu.be/OBwWCxG9SqM?t=1807) Late-round rookie picks are for chasing upside, but be quick to move on when they do not pan out.
  > "those late picks they don't work out to use them by all means. We're hunting upside. But be quick to move on."
